negotiable.label: Ask before you sign
negotiable.askIntro: Before you sign, ask the landlord in writing for:

consequence.scale: Ranked from 1, the clause that can cost you the most.

clauses.heading: 6B. Operating Cost Escalation
clauses.legalTextNote: Paste two or three sentences from your copy of sec. 6B. Do not paste the whole section.
clauses.findStart: The LESSEE shall pay to the LESSOR as additional rent
plain: You must pay a set percentage of any increase in the building's operating costs above the base year. You pay this on top of your base rent.
Operating costs include insurance, repairs, snow removal, staff pay, and some building improvements.
The lease sets no limit on how much this amount can rise.
clauses.cardLine: Your rent can rise when building costs rise.

clauses.heading: 13. Assignment - Subleasing
clauses.legalTextNote: Paste two or three sentences from your copy of sec. 13. Do not paste the whole section.
clauses.findStart: The LESSEE shall not assign or sublet
clauses.findEnd: covenants and conditions of this lease.
plain: You must get the landlord's written consent before you sublet the space or transfer the lease to someone else.
The lease does not say the landlord needs a reason to refuse.
If the landlord consents, you must still pay all the rent and keep every other promise in the lease.
clauses.cardLine: If you sublet, you still owe all the rent.

clauses.heading: 19. Default and Bankruptcy
clauses.legalTextNote: Paste two or three sentences from your copy of sec. 19. Do not paste the whole section.
clauses.findStart: The LESSEE shall default in the payment of any installment of rent
clauses.findEnd: during the residue of the term.
plain: When this applies: you have not paid rent 10 days after the landlord gives you written notice, or you have not fixed another broken promise in the lease 30 days after written notice.
What the landlord may do: end the lease, take back the space, and remove your belongings.
What you must still pay: the rent the landlord loses for the rest of the lease term, and the landlord's cost of fixing the problem, including lawyer's fees, plus interest.
This section also covers bankruptcy. Read sec. 19 for those terms.
clauses.cardLine: Late rent can cost you the space, and you still owe the rent.
